PullRequest.Title: nes: let settings and experiments override baked strategy values
PullRequest.Body:
Follow-up to #332018 / #332316, addressing two problems with the `patchBased02Optimized` strategy.

Originally this was structured as a revert of e845953 plus a re-land. That is no longer possible: #332802 and its follow-ups have since merged on top of e845953, so reverting would take a colleague's merged work with it and leaves four commits that do not compile. The change is now expressed directly on top of current `main`, with the same end state.

## 1. Model configuration outranked settings and experiments

Every baked knob was read as `modelConfig.x ?? getExperimentBasedConfig(x)`. Since `getExperimentBasedConfig` already resolves **user setting → experiment treatment → default**, putting the model configuration first placed it above *both*. Once a strategy baked a knob in, neither the user nor a flight could move it, and an A/B arm assigning one of these settings measured nothing.

Reads now go through `resolveModelConfigValue`:

> user setting → experiment treatment → **model configuration** → setting default

This needed a new configuration primitive, `getExperimentBasedConfigIfSet`, which reports only an explicitly provided value instead of falling back to the default — that is what makes "is this setting actually driven?" answerable. Registration-time reads use the observable form, since an imperative read inside an `autorun` would not subscribe and would miss a treatment arriving after the graph was built.

## 2. Two definitions of "unified" that could disagree

`supportsUnifiedCompletions` was resolved in `InlineEditProviderFeature` (for the provider `excludes`) and again per request in `InlineCompletionProviderImpl`. Nothing kept them in agreement, and disagreement is user-visible: if registration excludes the separate provider while a request declines to stand in for it, there is **no inline suggestion at all**. Both paths, plus the joint provider, now resolve through one `observeUnifiedCompletions`, which keeps the existing OR with the core `modelUnification` toggle.

## Also

- `defaultModelConfiguration()` applies `applyStrategyConfig`, so the `forceUseDefaultModel` (404) fallback stops silently dropping every baked knob.
- Renamed `patchBased02Optimized` → `patchBased02Unified`. "Optimized" did not say what the variant does; "unified" names its defining property and matches the existing `xtabUnifiedModel`. The wire value is renamed with the identifier — see the reviewer thread on this.
- Fixed a pre-existing bug where `updateExperimentBasedConfiguration` only matched `config.<fullyQualifiedId>`, so a treatment arriving under `copilotchat.config.<id>` never invalidated the setting's observers. This affects every existing `getExperimentBasedConfigObservable` consumer, not just this change, so it is a separate commit.

## Commits

Each compiles independently.

1. `configuration: refactor:` — hoist the duplicated treatment lookup into the base class (no behavior change)
2. `configuration: fix:` — invalidate observables for every treatment name a setting is published under
3. `configuration: feat:` — add `getExperimentBasedConfigIfSet`
4. `nes: fix:` — the precedence inversion, the single unified-completions definition, and the rename

## Known limitations

- **Flights win over baked values.** Experiments currently assigning these settings will override the strategy, so it only becomes self-contained for those users once those flights are retired. Values coincide today, so there is no behavior change.
- **Startup window (#332837) unchanged.** `supportsUnifiedCompletions` is the only baked value read at provider-registration time rather than per request, so on the fetched `/models` path there is a brief window before the model list resolves. Measured at ~600 ms against a real account.

## Testing

- `npm run typecheck --prefix extensions/copilot`, and each commit typechecks independently
- 2494 vitest tests pass across `platform/inlineEdits`, `platform/configuration`, `platform/proxyModels`, `extension/inlineEdits`, `extension/xtab`
- Ran a Code OSS build from these sources: the extension activates cleanly, and a local model configuration is accepted with `patchBased02Unified` and rejected with `patchBased02Optimized` (`Expected undefined, but got string`), confirming the rename end to end

Scenarios.Scenario: Extension activation and provider registration, including late /models and experimentation updates
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Initial provider/model construction and VS Code provider registration must complete before NES can serve requests. A later model-capability or explicit unification-setting change synchronously disposes and rebuilds the registration graph; recording cleanup is launched without awaiting it and is off the critical path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Register the inline completion provider with VS Code, and unregister the previous provider through disposal on a reactive rerun.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One registration per active provider mode initially, plus one replacement per actual model/core-unification/explicit-unification value change; joint and separate modes are mutually selected rather than both active.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Registration already reran for model-list capability and core unification changes. The diff additionally places explicit InlineEditsUnification setting/treatment changes on this path so registration and request behavior agree.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Registration is required before suggestions can be served; replacement is synchronous and bounded to a state change.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Read the recording directory and unlink matching old recording files when recording is disabled.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One directory read per registration autorun execution and one unlink per matching recording; the diff can add one execution when an explicit unification treatment/setting changes.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The cleanup operation and its placement in the registration autorun pre-existed; only the new explicit-unification dependency can cause an additional, infrequent rerun.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The call is fire-and-forget and therefore does not block registration or request progress.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Location: Transitive proxy model service feeding InlineEditsModelService._fetchedModelsObs
ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Fetch the model list whose update can change the selected model capability.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Existing model-list fetch behavior is unchanged; this diff consumes the resulting local observable and adds no fetch.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same /models update already drove onModelListUpdated and provider re-registration.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: A cold model list can affect the eventual registration choice, but the network boundary itself is not introduced or made more frequent by the diff.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Actual changes to the selected model, core unification state, or explicit unification setting/treatment; normally startup plus infrequent configuration/model changes, not keystrokes or rows.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Reactive autoruns dispose the previous reader store before rebuilding; no new parallel registration burst or unbounded queue is introduced. Asynchronous recording cleanup may overlap but gains at most one invocation per relevant state change.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Configuration observables are cached by accessor kind and setting ID; the selected-model capability is a derived observable. Cold model discovery may change the value once, while stable warm state performs no rebuild.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence in the added reactive dependency and one extra rebuild on an actual explicit-unification change; low evidence of material latency or sustained resource growth.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Constructor and registration cost is not benchmarked, and experiment refresh frequency varies, but the new trigger is bounded and infrequent and the filesystem work is off-path.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The diff can add a bounded provider replacement for a real configuration transition, but this is required to apply immutable registration options and does not create hot-path fan-out, unbounded retention, or blocking I/O.

Scenarios.Scenario: Typing-triggered inline edit request on a cold cache miss
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Request gating, delay calculation, prompt construction, debounce, then the existing model fetch must complete before a fresh suggestion is available. The changed resolution helpers execute before the existing debounce/network boundary.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Send the constructed inline-edit prompt to the model endpoint and consume its streamed response.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most the existing fetch per uncached logical request, subject to existing pending-request reuse, cancellation, debounce, and speculative-request behavior; the diff does not add a fetch or loop over inputs.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Cold misses already performed the same model request after debounce.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: This is the dominant cold-request critical path. The diff may intentionally alter configured debounce values but does not change fetch cardinality or scheduling absent an explicit setting/treatment override.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Keystroke/request frequency. Each changed resolver performs a constant number of local configuration/treatment lookups; prompt size, document count, and network request cardinality are unchanged.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Existing debounce, cancellation, live-dependent reuse, and speculative scheduling remain unchanged; no new Promise fan-out, queue, or unconstrained concurrency is added.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: A cold miss reaches one model request. Existing request/cache coalescing is unchanged. Baked strategy values remain the fallback on an unset configuration; only explicit user or experiment values supersede them.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence that the helper adds only bounded local reads and no new expensive boundary on this path.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: VS Code configuration inspection cost is not measured, but it is synchronous local state and the added count is constant against a request path that already reads many settings.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The added lookups are constant-size and implement the requested precedence without increasing network cardinality, prompt serialization scale, or concurrency.

Scenarios.Scenario: Warm cached suggestion response and cached-edit rendering
Scenarios.CriticalPath: A cache hit computes its minimum response delay and returns without a model fetch; rendering checks the resolved ghost-text behavior before exposing an existing suggestion.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: One constant-size model/config resolution per cache-delay or rendering decision; no work scales with cache size or document length.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Existing cache-hit delay and cancellation behavior are unchanged; no new asynchronous work is started.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Warm cache avoids the model network request as before. Cache keys, retention, eviction, rebasing, and coalescing are unchanged; explicit configuration can intentionally override baked cache-delay values.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence from the changed call sites in computeMinimumResponseDelay and the render suppression check.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The local inspection overhead is unmeasured but bounded to a few reads per returned cached suggestion.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. There is no cache defeat, retention increase, or scaling work; only constant local precedence resolution.

Scenarios.CriticalPath: After the existing model fetch starts yielding, parser options are resolved once before constructing the streaming response handler; the handler then processes streamed lines.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Existing model request and streamed response consumed by XtabPatchResponseHandler.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One stream per existing request/retry. The two changed option resolutions occur once per response, not once per streamed line or patch item.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same fetch and parser ran with baked values taking precedence over experiment/user values.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Network and parsing remain on the suggestion critical path; the diff adds only constant local option reads before parser construction.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Response line count controls existing parser work, but the added resolver work remains O(1) per response.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: The single response stream is consumed by the existing handler; no parallel parse or boundary calls are introduced.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Not cache-dependent after a cold fetch begins; changed option lookup does not alter response caching.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence that no repeated-work regression exists in the streaming path.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: No parser benchmark is available, but code placement proves the lookup is outside the per-line streaming loop.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The changed work does not scale with stream length and adds no boundary calls.

Scenarios.Scenario: Model-not-found fallback to the default inline-edit model
Scenarios.CriticalPath: After an existing model-not-found response, the provider retries using defaultModelConfiguration; the diff now applies the selected prompting strategy's local configuration before the retry is prepared.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Retry the model request with the default model after ModelNotFound.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: The existing single fallback retry behavior is unchanged; applying strategy configuration is local and does not add another retry.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The fallback already retried over the network, but defaultModelConfiguration returned the raw model configuration without applying baked strategy knobs.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The fallback network request remains on the critical path after a 404; the diff changes only local option values used by that request.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One fallback per model-not-found flow; configuration merge size is fixed and independent of document or model-list size.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: The fallback remains sequential after ModelNotFound; no additional concurrent request is introduced.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No new cache is introduced. The default model list is already held in observables; strategy application creates a bounded configuration object.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence from the fallback branch and defaultModelConfiguration change.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The latency effect of preserving individual strategy knobs is model/configuration dependent, but there is no mechanism increasing retry count or retained state.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The change preserves strategy defaults on an existing retry and does not add boundary fan-out or meaningful allocation scaling.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over all 24 changed files. Traced provider lifecycle, configuration invalidation, cold and warm inline-edit requests, streamed parsing, and model fallback. The diff adds bounded local configuration resolution and an infrequent registration refresh for explicit unification changes, but no high-confidence actionable performance regression, unbounded retention, cache defeat, or increased network/IPC fan-out was found.

Stats.CostNote: Copilot SDK reports nano-AI units and model billing multipliers; it does not provide a USD conversion.
